findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph and replace it with the actual policy for how requests are reviewed and who is responsible for approval.
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph
findings.violation: This describes a specific operational failure rather than policy procedure. It should not appear in a policy document.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Clarify whether managers must follow the standard review checklist or have discretionary authority. If discretion exists, specify its limits.
findings.violation: This contradicts the Approval Timeline section, which states "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list," implying managers must follow an approved list rather than exercise unrestricted discretion.

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.fix: Replace with clear, concise language: "The reimbursement offsets equipment costs the employee has already purchased."
findings.violation: The phrase "at this point in time" is vague and wordy, and the sentence restates the obvious rather than adding necessary information.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person: "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first sentence
findings.violation: Uses second person ("You" and "we"), while the rest of the document consistently uses third person, creating an inconsistent tone.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form."
findings.fix: Change to third person: "Employees record the stipend item on the request form."
findings.violation: Uses second person "You," inconsistent with the third-person perspective used throughout the document.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Change to third person: "Employees submit the request in the portal and track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.location: Terminology Notes section, last two sentences
findings.violation: Uses second person "you," inconsistent with the third-person perspective used throughout the document.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Remove this duplicate section and verify the correct publication schedule in the Program Overview.
findings.violation: This section duplicates and contradicts the Program Overview section. Program Overview states the log is published "each quarter," while this later section says "after every open enrollment period." These should not appear as separate sections.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
